column1: # TITLE: Acute high dose X-irradiation-induced genomic changes in a lung tumor cell line
# SUMMARY: Accidents with ionizing radiation (IR) often involve acute high dose exposures that can lead to acute radiation syndrome and late effects. IR can induce genomic lesions
column3: we investigated acute IR-induced cellular genomic signatures at the genome wide level. After exposing the adenocarcinoma cell line A549 to an acute 6 Gy 240 kV X-Ray dose
column4: four surviving clonogenic cells were recovered by minimal dilution and further expanded and analyzed by cytogenetics
column5: chromosome painting and tiling-path array CGH
column6: with the non-irradiated clone0 serving as control. It was found that acute X-ray exposure induced changes in modal chromosome number and specific translocations in the four irradiation surviving clones. Furthermore
column7: clone4 displayed an increased radiosensitivity at D > 5 Gy. Array CGH disclosed unique and recurrent genomic changes
column9: and disclosed fragile sites FRA3B and FRA16D as preferential regions of genomic alterations in all irradiated clones
column10: which likely relates to irradiation-induced genomic stress. Gene expression analysis revealed a specific profile of 364 genes in clone4
column11: of which p53 pathway genes may contribute to its increased radiosensitivity. IR-induced genomic changes AND fragile site expression highlight the capacity of a single acute radiation exposure to resculpture the genome of tumor cells by inflicting genomic stress.
